name: LLM-R (Learning to Retrieve In-Context Examples for Large Language Models)
venue: EACL 2024 (Findings/Main; accepted by EACL 2024). Preprint: arXiv:2307.07164 (v1 Jul 2023, v2 Jan 2024).
authors_affiliation: Liang Wang, Nan Yang, Furu Wei — all at Microsoft Research (Microsoft).
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/microsoft/LMOps (parent repo; the llm_retriever subdirectory hosts code and data).
task_domain: In-context example (demonstration) retrieval for LLMs across a broad suite of NLP tasks (Closed-book QA, commonsense reasoning, coreference, NLI, paraphrase, reading comprehension, sentiment, data-to-text, summarization). This is ICL demonstration retrieval, not agentic planning/tool-use.
problem_setting: Offline supervised setting: a single dense retriever is trained from frozen-LLM feedback to select few-shot in-context examples that maximize ICL performance. Supervision is available because each training example has a ground-truth output used to compute LLM log-likelihood feedback. Single-model (non-agent, non-interactive) setting; the trained retriever is then applied at test time to pick k-shot demonstrations from a static pool. A mixture of 30 tasks (9 categories) is trained jointly; 4 tasks are held out to test generalization to unseen tasks, and the retriever (trained with LLaMA-7B) is also tested for transfer to other LLMs (GPT-Neo-2.7B, LLaMA-13B, GPT-35-Turbo).
what_is_retrieved: Demonstrations (in-context examples) — i.e., (input x_i, output y_i) training pairs used as few-shot ICL exemplars.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: a fixed retrieval pool of ~6.3M labeled training examples (union of all training-task examples). The pool is frozen after construction; it is not a growing/episodic agent memory.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking objective: retrieve top-k (k=8 in main experiments) demonstrations by retriever similarity score. Candidates are treated independently (no minimal-set completeness or combinatorial selection); the paper notes in Limitations that joint/combinatorial selection of mutually-influencing examples is left to future work.
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve: yes, Reuse: yes (verbatim ICL exemplar), Revise: no, Retain: no]. Only Retrieve + Reuse phases are realized; no case adaptation/revision and no retention of new cases.
explicit_cbr_grounding: false — The work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner. It is framed as dense-retriever training for in-context example selection via reward-model knowledge distillation.
retrieval_unit: Single demonstration: one (input, output) example pair. The query is the test input x; each candidate key is the string concatenation of input x_i and output y_i.
index_source: Static corpus, offline-induced: the retrievable store is the union of all training examples (~6.3M) across the 30-task mixture, built once offline. No online/test-time growth.
index_structure_topology: Flat vector index: bi-encoder embeddings of candidate (x_i,y_i) pairs retrieved by cosine similarity (kNN). BM25 inverted index is used only as the initial/first-iteration retriever. No graph/hierarchical/cluster topology.
retriever_type: Learned dense bi-encoder (initialized from E5-base), trained via knowledge distillation from a cross-encoder reward model. BM25 (unsupervised) is the initial retriever for the first training iteration. So: hybrid pipeline (BM25 bootstrap) but the final deployed retriever is a learned dense bi-encoder.
retriever_learning_signal: LM-feedback + downstream-task-effectiveness via reward distillation. Pipeline: (1) BM25 retrieves top-n candidates; (2) a frozen LLM (LLaMA-7B) ranks candidates by log p(y | x, x_i, y_i) — the LM-feedback signal; (3) a cross-encoder reward model (ELECTRA-base) is trained with a softmax cross-entropy (1 positive vs N_neg hard negatives) over LLM-ranked candidates; (4) the bi-encoder retriever is trained by KL-divergence knowledge distillation from the reward model plus an InfoNCE contrastive loss (L = alpha*L_cont + L_distill). Trained iteratively (retriever from iter i mines candidates for iter i+1). Not RL; not a sequential decision policy.
query_construction: Raw test input x is used directly as the query (no decomposition, no synthetic/expanded query, no thought conditioning). At training time the query is the training input x and itself is excluded from retrieval results.
query_granularity: Task-level / instance-level, one-shot at t=0: a single query is formed from the test input and retrieval happens once before generation. No step-level or trajectory-level re-querying.
when_to_retrieve: One-shot: retrieve top-k demonstrations once per test input before the single LLM forward pass. (The 'iterative' aspect refers to iterative offline retriever TRAINING, not iterative test-time retrieval.)
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: retrieval is always performed once per test input (always-on, k=8). No confidence/uncertainty/learned-router trigger.
reranking: No test-time reranking stage. A cross-encoder reward model is used only during training (as a teacher for distillation, with access to ground-truth label y); it is not applied at inference. At test time the bi-encoder directly produces the top-k.
retrieved_context_refinement: None at test time: retrieved demonstrations are concatenated verbatim as k-shot prompt context. No decomposition, distillation, distractor filtering, or compression of retrieved items.
tool_document_engineering: N/A — no tool/skill descriptions; retrieved units are labeled NLP demonstrations, indexed as raw concatenated (x_i,y_i) strings (no synthetic-query augmentation or weighted-field embeddings).
index_content_separation: N/A — no separation of a lightweight index from heavy on-demand content; embeddings index the full (x_i,y_i) pairs directly.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A — not a tool-retrieval system; static example pool, no live tool index or integration protocol (RapidAPI/REST/MCP/function-calling).
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A — no inter-tool dependency modeling; demonstrations are treated independently.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: the top-k retrieved (input, output) pairs are concatenated as few-shot in-context examples in front of the test input and fed to the frozen LLM, which generates the prediction. The retrieved examples are also a training signal for the retriever offline, but at inference they are pure prompt exemplars.
planning_integration: N/A for planning — this is ICL demonstration retrieval, not a planner/agent. Integration pattern: one-shot retrieve-then-prompt (retrieve top-k exemplars at prompt-construction time, then a single LLM forward pass for the answer). No interleaving with planning, MCTS, or a search loop.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-answer: a single retrieval informs a single LLM prediction for the whole test instance. No per-step / per-token / per-tool-call interleaving.
adaptation_mechanism: Verbatim ICL exemplar: retrieved demonstrations are reused as-is in the prompt with no adaptation/revision (consistent with CBR Retrieve+Reuse only).
retrieved_item_representation: Raw demonstration text: each injected item is the verbatim (input, output) training pair rendered with the task template. No distilled strategy, workflow, executable program, or latent/soft tokens.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Single demonstration (raw, concrete input-output example). Not a distilled strategy, guideline, workflow, or skill.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Retriever-aware training via reward-model distillation and hard-negative mining: the cross-encoder reward model provides fine-grained, lower-variance supervision (vs raw LLM log-likelihood) and iterative training mines better positives/hard-negatives, improving the retriever's ability to discriminate helpful vs unhelpful examples. No explicit test-time relevance evaluator, self-reflection, or distractor filtering.
memory_type: none — static labeled example pool used as a retrieval corpus; no episodic/skill/workflow/procedural/graph/latent memory that the system writes to.
write_back: false — the system does not store new experiences/cases/skills; the retrieval pool is fixed (the union of training examples) and is not augmented at deployment.
online_growth: No — the retrievable store is frozen after offline construction; it does not grow during deployment/test-time.
write_back_trigger: never — no write-back mechanism exists; nothing is added to the pool during or after inference.
failure_experience_usage: Success-only / label-driven (no failure-experience memory). During TRAINING, hard NEGATIVE (low-LLM-feedback) candidates are mined and used contrastively to train the reward model and retriever, so negative/less-helpful examples shape the retriever; but there is no storage or retrieval of failed task trajectories as experiences. The retrieval pool contains only ground-truth labeled examples.
memory_evolution_update: N/A / append-only-at-train-time only: the example pool is static (no mutation). The only iterative update is offline retriever-parameter refinement across training iterations (mining better positives/negatives), not mutation of stored entries.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Partially: retrieval is a LEARNED scoring function (dense bi-encoder distilled from a reward model trained on LLM feedback), so selection is learned rather than a fixed off-the-shelf similarity. However it is NOT an RL/sequential-decision policy (no M-MDP, no soft Q-learning); it is a learned top-k similarity retriever with independent candidate scoring.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: N/A — single-retriever, single-model setting; no multi-agent or cross-framework memory sharing. (The retriever does generalize/transfer across different evaluation LLMs, but that is model transfer, not shared memory.)
benchmarks: 30 publicly available datasets across 9 categories (collection based on FLAN and UPRISE): Closed-book QA (CQA), Commonsense reasoning, Coreference, NLI, Paraphrase, Reading Comprehension, Sentiment, Data-to-text (D2T), Summarization. Specific datasets mentioned include NQ, ARC (easy/challenge), HellaSwag, COPA, PAWS, OpenBookQA, WSC, Winogrande, MultiRC, SNLI, MNLI, SQuAD v1, Sentiment140; 4 held-out tasks: QNLI, PIQA, WSC273, Yelp.
benchmark_family: QA / general NLP (FLAN-style task suite) — closed-book QA, commonsense, coreference, NLI, paraphrase, reading comprehension, sentiment, data-to-text, summarization. Not web/embodied/tool/code/memory/decision-RL families.
baselines: Zero-shot prompting, Random selection, K-means clustering, BM25, off-the-shelf dense retrievers E5-base and SBERT (all-mpnet-base-v2), and EPR (Efficient Prompt Retrieval, Rubin et al. 2022; re-implemented for fair comparison). A REPLUG-style variant (LLM log-likelihood as distillation reward) is compared as an ablation.
key_metrics: Task-specific metrics averaged per category and overall (accuracy for classification/multiple-choice; ROUGE/BLEU-style for generation tasks like D2T/summarization). Reported as average score across the 30 tasks (and per-category averages). Std dev over 3 runs reported for the Random baseline.
headline_result: On the 30-task suite with LLaMA-7B and 8 in-context examples, LLM-R reaches an average score of 66.5 (2 iterations), vs 63.5 for the best baseline EPR and 61.3 for BM25 — i.e., +3.0 over the strongest retrieval baseline (EPR) and roughly +8.6 over Random (57.9). On the 4 held-out unseen tasks it averages 81.7, surpassing the second-best (E5-base, 76.3) by +5.4 points.
ablations: Training-pipeline ablations (Table 2, 1-iter LLM-R = 65.7): (1) 'w/o reward model' (contrastive loss only on LLM-ranked candidates) drops to 64.9 (-0.8), showing the reward model is crucial; (2) 'reward model w/o label y+' (reward model lacks ground-truth label) drops to 63.8 (-1.9), the largest drop, showing label access for the teacher matters; (3) 'LLM score as reward' (REPLUG-style log-likelihood as distillation target) gives 65.2 (-0.5), worse because raw LLM log-likelihood is high-variance/not a proper distribution; (4) initializing retriever with BERT-base instead of E5-base gives 65.2 (-0.5). Iterative training: 1 iter 65.7 -> 2 iter 66.5 -> 3 iter 66.4 (converges after 2). Generalization to LLMs: GPT-Neo-2.7B +7.4, LLaMA-13B +4.2, GPT-35-Turbo +0.4 over BM25 (gains larger for smaller LLMs). Ranking-LLM vs eval-LLM (Table 6): eval LLM quality is the primary determinant; ranking-LLM choice has minor impact; merging both training sources is marginally best. Scaling: gains diminish after ~4 in-context examples; large-size retriever boosts more than small/base.
evaluation_decoupling: No — only end-to-end downstream ICL task metrics are reported; intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG) are not reported separately. Retrieval quality is assessed indirectly via downstream task performance and qualitative retrieved-example analysis.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Outcome-only: evaluation scores the final task prediction. There is qualitative analysis of retrieved examples (similar input patterns; when LLM-R helps vs hurts, e.g., low diversity on SQuAD) but no quantitative process/faithfulness metric.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Efficiency motivations: bi-encoder used for fast inference; computing LLM feedback log p(y|x,x_i,y_i) needs only one forward pass per candidate (no task-specific metric). Scaling analysis shows gains diminish after ~4 examples (more examples => longer prompts, higher inference cost); small-size retriever is comparable to base-size (cheaper deployment option). No explicit latency/API-cost numbers reported.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k: 8 in-context examples retrieved per test input in main experiments (k held constant). Scaling experiment varies k (gains saturate after ~4). No adaptive/budget-capped/precision-driven selection.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A — primary method paper, not a survey.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A — not a benchmark-construction paper; it reuses 30 public datasets (collection based on FLAN and UPRISE). Pool ~6.3M examples; up to 30k train / 10k eval sampled per dataset.
builds_on: EPR (Efficient Prompt Retrieval, Rubin et al. 2022) for LLM-feedback-trained ICL retrieval; E5 (Wang et al. 2022) retriever initialization; ELECTRA (Clark et al. 2020) reward-model init; iterative dense-retrieval training (ANCE/Xiong et al. 2021; Li et al. 2023); knowledge distillation from a cross-encoder teacher; InfoNCE contrastive learning (Chen et al. 2020 / SimCLR). REPLUG (Shi et al. 2023) is the inspiration for the LLM-log-likelihood-reward variant. Task collection based on FLAN (Wei et al. 2022) and UPRISE (Cheng et al. 2023).
contrasts_with: Contrasts with off-the-shelf / unsupervised retrievers (BM25, SBERT, E5, K-means, Random) that use similarity only; with EPR which distills directly from LLM scores per task; with REPLUG-style direct LLM-log-likelihood distillation (shown suboptimal because the signal is high-variance and not a proper distribution); with UPRISE (cross-task retrieval) and FLAN (instruction fine-tuning) whose objectives differ. Distinguished from ad-hoc retrieval re-rankers since the reward model uses the ground-truth label y unavailable at test time.
lineage: Group A — ICL demonstration retrieval. A learned, LLM-feedback-trained dense retriever for selecting in-context examples; a successor to KATE/EPR-style learned demonstration retrievers, adding a cross-encoder reward model + iterative knowledge distillation for multi-task, generalizable ICL example retrieval.
